principles: Camera only advances when the player presses right past the lead zone.
World progress never rewinds; left/back movement is limited to a few meters of tactical repositioning.
Engagements become wider arena locks with cover, vertical props, and readable enemy tells.
Sprites stay large, but the playable lane is wider so dodging, crouching, and cover choices have room to breathe.

pacingRules: Use player-led rightward camera advancement instead of constant auto-scroll so players can read threats before committing.
Keep a short backward allowance on screen, but never rewind world progress once the camera has advanced.
Keep 0–4 enemies on screen; prefer fewer enemies with stronger tells over spam.
Reduce enemy movement speed and rate of fire so crouch/cover/jump decisions matter.
Enemy melee counters should lag player melee by roughly 1–2 seconds after a readable tell.
Use destructible cover, explosive props, platforms, and ground gaps to create tactical decisions.
Scroll resumes only after staged enemies, mini-bosses, or bosses are cleared.

enemyAiFairness.readableTellRule: Every damaging action must spend telegraph frames on-screen before collision or projectile release.
enemyAiFairness.roleCapRule: Prefer fewer active attackers with stronger tells; staged rooms should not dogpile more than two simultaneous attacks.

nextBalanceQuestions: Does rightward pressure advance the room quickly enough without feeling like auto-scroll?
Can a new player identify safe crouch-cover positions before the first enemy shot?
Are enemy tell frames visible for melee and ranged attacks before damage lands?
Do explosive barrels solve crowd pressure without trivializing waves?
Can the player exit back to Lester’s Arcade from pause or game-over without confusion?
